::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
This list is compiled and ranked each month by Claude, an AI model made by
Anthropic, running unattended. No person reviews the entries or the scores
before they are published. Criteria was set in.
[Specification 2](specification2-curated-list.qmd) and does not adjust
individual scores.
:::

Every score runs from 0 to 100. The full definitions are in
[Specification 2](specification2-curated-list.qmd), Section 4.
The scores capture:

- **S** The total of the other scores.
- **Q** Quality
- **E** Expertise
- **M** Maintenance and usability 
- **U** Usage 

Grouping:

- Only skills with evidence of use are ranked.
- **Flags.** ❌ a major error found. ⚠️ no licence, archived repository, authors
  not found in OpenAlex, or an author matched by name alone.
- **At most three skills per library are ranked in each category.** 

## Tool Skills

Skills for particular software tools (e.g. NONMEM, Monolix, nlimxr2)

::: {#tool-skills}
:::

## Task Skills

Skills whose instructions hold across tools (e.g. Model Evaluation)

::: {#task-skills}
:::

## Unproven

Skills scored on everything except use, in order of their total, with no
evidence yet that anyone outside their authors has used them. A skill moves up
to the ranked tables in the month that evidence appears.

::: {#unproven}
:::

## Evaluation Resources

Test cases and benchmarks for measuring how well an assistant does
pharmacometrics work. Not ranked: Specification 2 does not yet define a quality
score for them.

::: {#evaluation-resources}
:::

## This Month's Run

**October 2026**, run on 2026-10-07, and reissued the same day under criteria
version 2, which replaced adoption with use and ranks only skills with evidence
of use. Five of the 40 skills have that evidence. Discovery searched
GitHub code and repositories with the queries in [`discovery.yml`](https://github.com/iamstein/TrinityMetrics/blob/main/projects/ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/discovery.yml), cloned 25
repositories and scored 40 skills. Copies were merged into their originals: 37
copies of K-Dense's `pkpd-modeling` alone. Exclusions and copies are listed in
[`list/2026-10.yml`](https://github.com/iamstein/TrinityMetrics/blob/main/projects/ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/list/2026-10.yml).

**Four skills were added on 2026-10-09, outside the run, at Andy's request.**
Discovery missed [nlmixr2/AI-assisted-MIDD](https://github.com/nlmixr2/AI-assisted-MIDD),
an NCA, popPK and simulation project template created six days before the run.
Its three analysis skills and its data-validation skill were scored by the same
criteria, in the same single pass. The other 14 skills in the repository are
the database, logging, report and QC steps around those four, and were not
scored. The four have no evidence of use yet, so they are listed under
Unproven.

**Both known-answer checks passed.** The error audit reported both errors in
[`fixtures.yml`](https://github.com/iamstein/TrinityMetrics/blob/main/projects/ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/fixtures.yml) as major before anything was scored.

This first run departs from the specification in four ways:

1. **One scoring pass.** The rubric and the error audit were each run once, by
   the same model. The second independent pass, the judge-agreement figure and
   the test-retest correlation were not produced, so a difference of a few
   points between two skills is within the noise of a single judgement.
2. **Large libraries were pre-screened.** In libraries of 30 or more skills, the
   most pharmacometric skills were chosen by keyword before scoring, and the
   per-library cap applied to those.
3. **No benchmark score.** No evaluation resource yet covers a listed skill's
   task with expected findings.
4. **Use is measured from GitHub issues, pull requests, comments and
   installations only.** GitHub Discussions were not searched, and no listed
   skill ships in a package with download statistics.

## Proposed Changes to the Criteria

The run proposes these for Andy to accept or reject in [`criteria.yml`](https://github.com/iamstein/TrinityMetrics/blob/main/projects/ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/criteria.yml) and
[`rubric.md`](https://github.com/iamstein/TrinityMetrics/blob/main/projects/ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/rubric.md). Until he does, the criteria stay as they are.

1. **Add a rubric item for domain content.** A templated review skill with no
   named diagnostic meets most of the current items, so it scores close to a
   skill that explains how to read a VPC. An item such as "names at least five
   specific diagnostics or methods and says how to read each" would separate
   them.
2. **Add a rubric item for verified output.** Some tool skills require the
   assistant to check its result numerically before reporting it, such as a
   converted model reproducing the original engine's predictions. The rubric
   gives that no credit.
3. **Define a score for evaluation resources**, from the number of test cases
   with expected answers and the tasks they cover, so the third category can be
   ranked.
4. **Decide how organisations count for expertise.** Skills published under an
   organisation or a bot account score 0 on E, however expert the team. A
   named-author list, where the organisation publishes one, could stand in.
